metaDescription: Seven over-ear noise cancelling headphones compared on ANC design, comfort, battery claims and ownership, with picks for flights, commutes and tight budgets.
expertTake: The Sony WH-1000XM6 is our top pick for people who want the strongest noise cancelling and a feature-rich app, and the JBL Tune 780NC is the value pick for anyone who mostly wants quiet on a commute. If you only listen in a quiet room or exercise outdoors where awareness matters, skip the category and buy ordinary open or transparent-leaning headphones instead.
introParagraphs: Noise cancelling headphones do one job very well: they take the steady drone of engines, air conditioning and road noise and turn it into a faint hush. They do far less for voices, keyboards and sudden sounds, which is where expectations and reality part ways.

Over-ear models also differ in comfort over hours, battery honesty, call quality and how long the pads and battery survive. This guide compares seven over-ear options on those ownership details so you can match a design to your actual day, not a feature list.

products.name: Sony WH-1000XM6 wireless over-ear ANC headphones
products.description:
Sony builds the WH-1000XM6 around a dedicated noise cancelling processor called the QN3 and an array of twelve microphones, which is the most microphone-heavy layout in this lineup. More microphones give the system more data about outside sound, and that is why this model is positioned as the strongest canceller here. The headband and cushioning are soft, and the earcups are shaped to spread clamping force rather than concentrate it.

The tradeoff is that the headphones sit at the top of the price ladder in this comparison, tier ten of ten on our scale, so you pay for the processing and the polish. Next to the Bose QuietComfort Headphones, which rely on a simpler microphone layout and a lower price tier, the Sony gains the LDAC codec and a deeper app, but the Bose is easier to set up and just as relaxed on the head. If you only stream from an iPhone over AAC, LDAC adds nothing, and the extra cost buys less.

In ownership terms, the XM6 is a headphone for people who live in the companion app, where you adjust ANC strength, equalizer and ambient behaviour. Expect the synthetic leather pads to wear after two to three years of daily use, and plan on replacement pads rather than a new pair. The built-in battery will lose capacity over several hundred cycles, and it is not meant to be changed by the user, so wired listening over the 3.5 mm cable is a useful backup for the end of the headphone's life.
products.bestFor: Frequent flyers and commuters who want the strongest cancelling and deep app control.
pros: Twelve microphones and a dedicated processor target engine and traffic drone
LDAC support suits Android listeners who care about codec choice
Folding design and a wired option make travel easier
Deep app lets you tune ANC strength, ambient mode and EQ
cons: Highest price tier here, hard to justify for casual listening
LDAC and some extras do nothing for a plain iPhone user
Strong cancelling can give some people a pressure sensation

products.name: Bose QuietComfort Headphones (2nd Gen) over-ear ANC
products.description:
The second generation of the QuietComfort Headphones keeps the Bose approach: a simple set of listening modes, soft synthetic leather and a design built around hours of wear rather than a dense feature sheet. The newer headband is wider than the previous generation and uses more of the soft padded material, which spreads the weight over a larger area of the scalp. A pill-shaped earcup design replaces the older look, and Bose adds TrueSpatial processing for a more open sound.

The compromise is control depth. Compared with the Sony WH-1000XM6, which offers twelve microphones and a long list of ANC and equalizer adjustments, the Bose gives you two modes, Quiet and Aware, and a lighter app experience. That is a strength for people who want to press one button and forget it, and a weakness for tinkerers. It also costs less than the Sony, so the question is whether the Bose approach suits you better.

In use, the second generation charges over USB-C, which keeps one cable in your bag for the phone and the headphones. Plan for ear pad wear after two to three years, and check that replacement pads are sold for your model before you rely on that plan. Like every model here, the internal battery fades with age, so treat the headphones as a three to four year purchase and not a lifetime one.
products.bestFor: Long flights and workdays where fit and simplicity matter more than deep tuning.
pros: Wider padded headband spreads weight for long wear sessions
Quiet and Aware modes keep daily use simple and fast
TrueSpatial processing adds a more open soundstage on music
USB-C charging means one cable for phone and headphones
cons: Fewer tuning options than the Sony for people who like to adjust
Still a high price tier for casual listening
Synthetic pads still wear over several years of daily use

products.name: Beats Studio Pro over-ear ANC headphones, USB-C audio
products.description:
Beats designs the Studio Pro around a custom acoustic platform and active noise cancelling, with a Transparency mode for letting speech and announcements through. Its standout hardware detail is USB-C audio, which lets you plug in a cable and listen with lossless audio support from compatible devices. The headband is padded and the cups are closed, so passive isolation supports the active system.

The tradeoff is that the 40 hour claim is a best case, and listing language for headphones like this usually refers to listening with cancelling off. With ANC on, expect a lower figure, and with heavy volume lower still. It also costs less than the Sony and the second-generation Bose, sitting at tier five here, but it does not match their cancelling strength on owner feedback patterns, and some features work most fully with Apple devices.

Setup is easy on an iPhone, where pairing is near instant, and it works with Android too. Over time, expect the pads to flake after two to three years and the battery to fade after several hundred cycles. A hard travel case helps protect the folding hinges, and cleaning the pads with a damp cloth every few weeks keeps skin oils from degrading the surface early.
products.bestFor: iPhone owners who want easy pairing, a wired USB-C option and a mid-priced tier.
pros: USB-C wired mode supports lossless listening from compatible devices
Fast Fuel charging gives hours of use from a short plug-in
Easy one-touch pairing for iPhone and Apple accounts
Padded band and closed cups give solid passive isolation
cons: Cancelling is less strong than the Sony or newer Bose on owner reports
Forty hour claim is with ANC off, so real use is shorter
Some features work fully only with Apple devices

products.name: JBL Tune 780NC adaptive ANC over-ear, up to 76 h
products.description:
The JBL Tune 780NC is a budget-conscious over-ear that pairs adaptive noise cancelling with a Smart Ambient mode and a bass-forward JBL tuning. Adaptive ANC adjusts the amount of cancelling to the sound around you, so you are not choosing a fixed level on a noisy street and a quiet office. Two microphones with beamforming handle call pickup, which is a simpler setup than the flagships.

The tradeoff is performance at the top end. Compared with the Soundcore Q20i, which sits in the lowest price tier here and claims 40 hours with ANC on, the JBL claims up to 76 hours, but that figure is likely measured with cancelling off. Compared with the Sony WH-1000XM6, which has twelve microphones, the JBL cancels less and has weaker call pickup, which matters on a crowded train.

In ownership, this is a low-risk purchase because the price tier is third lowest, but plan on plastic parts and softer pads that will show wear after about two years. The battery is sealed, and the Bluetooth connection is stable for streaming. For the money, it is the best answer to the question of whether you need to spend more than a few tiers up the scale.
products.bestFor: Commuters and students who want real ANC and long battery at a modest tier.
pros: Adaptive ANC adjusts to the room without manual changes
Seventy-six hour listing leaves room even with ANC on
Smart Ambient mode lets announcements through when needed
Low price tier compared with the Sony, Bose and Beats models
cons: Cancelling is clearly weaker than the Sony and Bose flagships
Call pickup with two microphones struggles in crowded places
Plastic build and soft pads age faster than premium models

products.name: Soundcore Q20i hybrid ANC over-ear, 40 h with ANC
products.description:
Soundcore, the audio brand of Anker, designs the Q20i with hybrid active noise cancelling that uses four built-in microphones to filter background sound. A BassUp mode adds low end for people who like punchy music, and a wired mode keeps it working with the battery flat. The construction is lightweight plastic with soft cushions, aimed at everyday budget buyers.

The compromise is fine detail and cancelling strength. Next to the JBL Tune 780NC, the Soundcore's 40 hour claim is with ANC on, which is a more honest listing than a bigger number measured with ANC off, but it trades some of the JBL's extra ambient features. It sits at tier two on our price scale, which is the second-cheapest of the seven, so the savings against the Bose and Sony models are large, and so are the gaps in cancelling depth and call quality.

Setup is simple, and the companion app offers an equalizer. Expect the plastic hinges and pads to be the first wear points, and keep it out of a loaded backpack that could stress the folding hinge. After about two years, plan for pad replacement, and check that your region sells replacements before you buy.
products.bestFor: First-time ANC buyers who want a low entry tier and honest battery wording.
pros: Battery claim is stated with cancelling on, which is more realistic
Four microphones give hybrid ANC at a very low price tier
Short top-up charge adds listening time when the battery runs out
Wired mode keeps working even when the battery is empty
cons: Cancelling and call pickup trail every flagship in this lineup

buyingCriteria.criterion: How strong the ANC really is
buyingCriteria.explanation: Active noise cancelling works by listening with microphones and playing an inverse wave, so it is strongest on steady low-frequency sounds like engines and fans and weak on voices. The Sony WH-1000XM6 uses twelve microphones and a QN3 processor, while the Soundcore Q20i uses four, and that difference is visible in how far each can smooth a busy environment. A common mistake is assuming a higher microphone count removes speech; it does not. Treat strong ANC as relief for hum, not silence.

Weight and clamp force decide whether headphones are pleasant on hour four of a flight. Over-ear models in this range commonly weigh about 250 to 350 grams, and a wider headband like the one on the Bose QuietComfort Headphones (2nd Gen) spreads that load. People who wear glasses should look for softer, deeper pads, because stiff cups press the frame arms into the side of the head. Try to buy from a retailer with a generous return window for this reason.

Battery numbers are measured at moderate volume, and big claims usually mean cancelling off. Buyers get caught when a 100 hour badge turns into a much smaller number with ANC enabled. Expect to charge every week or two with daily use, whatever the box says.

Codecs decide how audio is compressed over Bluetooth, and the real-world gain is small compared with tuning and fit. SBC is the baseline, AAC suits iPhones, and LDAC on the Sony WH-1000XM6 helps Android users. Hi-Res on a listing without a named codec is a label, not a spec. A wired mode matters more than people think, because the Beats Studio Pro lets you plug in over USB-C and every model here has a way to listen when the battery is empty.

Headphones that cancel well do not always sound good to the person on the other end. Call quality depends on beamforming microphones and wind handling, and the JBL Tune 780NC uses two microphones for calls while the Sony uses twelve overall. Transparency or Aware modes also differ: the Bose Quiet and Aware pair is simple, while Beats offers Transparency. If you take many calls on trains, weigh this more than the ANC depth.

The battery is sealed in every model here, and lithium cells fade after several hundred cycles, so a three to four year life is a reasonable expectation. Pads wear sooner, in roughly two to three years, and brands with replaceable pads extend the life of the product. A named brand tends to have clearer warranty and spare-part availability.

specDecoder.meaning: Hybrid systems use microphones on the outside of the cup and inside near the ear. The combination handles a wider range of noise than a single set of microphones.
specDecoder.watchFor: A budget model like the Soundcore Q20i uses four microphones, so hybrid on a low tier is real but shallower than the Sony's twelve.

specDecoder.meaning: The number is measured at a moderate volume, usually in a mode that helps the figure. Real life with cancelling on and louder listening is lower.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 76 hour claim on the JBL Tune 780NC is a best case, while the Soundcore Q20i states 40 hours with ANC on.

specDecoder.meaning: A codec is the compression method between phone and headphones. SBC is universal, AAC suits Apple, and LDAC and aptX serve Android.
specDecoder.watchFor: LDAC on the Sony WH-1000XM6 is only useful with a phone that also supports it.

specDecoder.meaning: Multipoint lets the headphones stay connected to two devices at once, such as a laptop and a phone. It saves repairing every time you switch.
specDecoder.watchFor: Check the listing for each lineup model, because support varies and some budget units skip it.

specDecoder.meaning: Weight is listed in grams, and clamp force is rarely stated at all. Together they decide comfort, and the headband design matters more than a gram or two.
specDecoder.watchFor: The wider headband of the Bose QuietComfort Headphones (2nd Gen) is the clearest design answer to long-wear fatigue in this lineup.

howWeEvaluated.title: ANC hardware and approach
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated how each model builds its noise cancelling, from the microphone count to the processor. The Sony WH-1000XM6 lists twelve microphones, the Soundcore Q20i lists four, and the rest fall in between. We read this alongside published specifications, not lab measurements.

howWeEvaluated.title: Comfort and fit design
howWeEvaluated.description: We researched headband width, cushion material and typical weights. We weighted designs that spread load, like the wider headband on the Bose second generation, and compared them with plainer plastic builds. Comfort scores are editorial assessments, not measurements.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery honesty
howWeEvaluated.description: We read each battery claim for the condition it assumes. We favoured honest wording over bigger figures.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership and repair
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at the realities of year three: pad wear, sealed batteries and wired fallback. Based on patterns in owner feedback, pads are the first part to age, and replacement availability separates named brands from small makers.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value within the tier
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared each model with its closest neighbours on a relative price scale, with tier one the cheapest. We weighed the Beats Studio Pro at tier five against the Sony at tier ten for what the extra spend actually buys.

cards.label: Sony WH-1000XM6
cards.text: Offers twelve microphones, LDAC and a deep app with many adjustments. It rewards people who like to tune, and it folds for travel.

cards.label: Bose QuietComfort (2nd Gen)
cards.text: Offers a wider headband, TrueSpatial audio and two simple modes. It rewards people who want to wear it and forget it.

howToChoose.note: Pick the Sony if you listen over Android with LDAC or like adjusting ANC; pick the Bose if comfort and simplicity come first.

rows: Listing of up to 76 hours leaves headroom with ANC on
Claim of 40 hours is stated with ANC on

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Strong low-frequency cancelling, a wired option, a hard case and a comfortable headband. Pressure sensation from strong ANC is personal, so a return window matters.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Sony WH-1000XM6 and Bose QuietComfort Headphones (2nd Gen) lead on engine drone and comfort. The Beats Studio Pro adds a USB-C wired option for seat-back connections.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You fly often, work in loud open spaces or take many calls. The Sony WH-1000XM6 and Bose second generation are built for those jobs.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You commute for under an hour or mostly want quiet at home. The JBL Tune 780NC and Soundcore Q20i give real ANC at much lower tiers.

maintenance.why: Skin oils and sweat break down synthetic leather over time. A slightly damp cloth slows flaking and keeps the seal that ANC depends on.
Worn pads let sound leak and weaken cancelling. Replace them at the first sign of cracks or flat spots.
Folding hinges and headbands are the most stressed parts. A hard case prevents crushing in a bag.
Brands tweak ANC and connection stability through updates. Keeping the app current also keeps multipoint working reliably.
Lithium cells age faster when stored empty or very hot. Keep a partial charge for long storage and avoid leaving them in a hot car.

faq.q: Are over-ear or earbuds better for noise cancelling?
faq.a: Over-ear headphones usually cancel low-frequency noise better because the cup adds passive isolation and room for more microphones. Earbuds win on portability. For flights and loud offices, over-ear is the safer pick.

faq.q: Do I need to spend a lot to get good ANC?
faq.a: No, but the strength of cancelling does rise with the price tier. The Soundcore Q20i and JBL Tune 780NC give real relief on engine and traffic noise. The Sony and Bose models go further on voices and variable sounds.

faq.q: How long do noise cancelling headphones last?
faq.a: A reasonable expectation is three to four years for the battery and two to three years for the pads. Replaceable pads extend the life. Named brands are easier to support than small makers.

faq.q: Does a higher battery number mean longer use?
faq.a: Not always. A claim with ANC on, like the Soundcore Q20i at 40 hours, is easier to trust.

faq.q: Is it safe to wear ANC headphones while walking or cycling?
faq.a: Cancelling reduces your awareness of traffic, so use Aware or Transparency mode outdoors and follow local rules. In many places, wearing them while cycling is discouraged. When in doubt, take one ear off.

faq.q: Do ANC headphones work with a wired connection?
faq.a: Most do, and it is useful on flights and when the battery dies. The Sony WH-1000XM6 and Bose QuietComfort models offer a cable option, and the Beats Studio Pro supports USB-C audio. Check the listing before relying on it.
